evidence.excerpt: This paper presents a structured procedure for dimensioning passive EMC input filters for variable-speed drives to meet IEC 61800-3 Category C2 quasi-peak limits. The procedure uses measured CM and DM source impedances and a target attenuation profile derived from the gap between unfiltered emission spectra and the regulatory limit line, with a 6 dB safety margin applied throughout. Filter topologies (LC, LCL, and CL stages) are compared for a 15 kW test drive, and component values are selected to avoid resonances within the 150 kHz–2 MHz band that could cause limit exceedances at intermediate frequencies. Prototype filters were wound on nanocrystalline toroidal cores and verified by insertion-loss measurement per IEC 60939-3 before integration. Final compliance measurements confirmed that all quasi-peak and average readings were at least 5 dB below the Category C2 limit across the full 150 kHz–30 MHz range. Total filter volume was 0.38 litres and mass 0.61 kg for the 15 kW case.
